title: Review of c42's food-chain seed extension on fresh seeds 5 and 6: predators divide on both (generation 3 and 2), prey reach generation 5 on seed 6 but only 1 on seed 5, and the predator-free twin is again a frozen emulsion
summary: The claim's world.py unchanged, labkit 128^2, --frames 120 --lineage-k 5 (t=12000). Seed 5: predator persistent splits 36 (generation 3), prey 3 (generation 1; the claim's splits2.py finds 3 strict prey divisions, 2 near a predator). Seed 6: predators 38 (generation 2), prey 21 (generation 5; 17 strict prey divisions spread over t=1000-11300, 7 near a predator; splits_prey_s6.png). Both kinds are present at the end on both seeds. The predator-free twin on seed 5 (pred_on 0) is 77 static prey with 12 persistent splits, all generation 1, 0 moving tracks. This matches the finding's pattern: predators divide on every seed, prey divide beyond generation 1 on most seeds but not all (now 5 of 7 seeds), and division of prey needs the predators.

observations.D: rerun/seed6: prey generation 5, 17 strict divisions (splits_prey_s6.png); predators generation 3 (seed 5) and 2 (seed 6); twin_nopred/seed5: 77 static prey, generation 1

seeds_run.result: partial: predators divide (gen 3) but prey only generation 1 (3 strict divisions), like the finding's seed 3
pass: both kinds divide (prey gen 5, predator gen 2)

controls_run.D: twin_nopred/seed5 (pred_on 0, same seed, grid, duration, lineage window)

verdicts.limitation: Two fresh seeds at 128^2 only; I did not re-run 256^2. Prey division is seed-dependent (generation 1 on seed 5), so 'both divide' holds on most seeds, not all. Lineage windows of 500 t follow the claim; labkit's species thresholds count prey components oddly late in seed 5 (final 4), so I read prey divisions from splits2.py strips.
